triage.note: PR #61 R10, and the owner's chosen fix — close the paid path at the door. R1's fixture exclusion did NOT close `intc-2025` as a money path: `POST /api/extract/url` accepts any `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/…` URL and reached the same `_run` with escalation on, and `intc-2025` is a real Intel EDGAR filing whose own Archives URL still billed. Fixture exclusion could never fix it — extracting arbitrary EDGAR URLs is the feature, and any collapsing filing on EDGAR was a paid call for an anonymous caller — so four disclosure sites saying 'an upload is the only route' were false. `src/sec10k/web/gate.py` is the door: escalation runs only for a request presenting a valid `X-Escalation-Token`, and with no `SEC10K_ESCALATION_TOKEN` configured it runs for NOBODY. This case is deliberately not another AST shape read. `gate.py` is stdlib-only and imports no fastapi precisely so this check can IMPORT it and run the whole decision table — unset secret, secret under `MIN_TOKEN_CHARS`, absent header, empty header, wrong header, disarmed deployment, and the one combination that opens. PR #58 R18, PR #61 R2 and PR #61 R11 are three separate evasions that each satisfied a shape and broke the property; a table that is executed cannot be satisfied that way. The remaining assertions are the CHOKE POINT, which is what R13 taught: `_run` is the only caller of `extract_items` in app.py and calls the door exactly once, `escalate=` and `budget=` are the same name (so a request cannot escalate on one condition and bill against another), `_run` takes a `request`, and `view['escalation']` is built from the verdict. Plus the page printing the server's own reason verbatim, because with the tier behind a token `routing: null` is now the common case and an absent strip lets a viewer conclude the tier ran and stayed quiet.
triage.note_negative_space: It does not prove fastapi binds the routes (the standing app.py limitation, TD-38), that the operator chose a good secret, or that a holder of the secret cannot spend — that is the process `Budget`'s job, and the budget is the ceiling BEHIND the door, not instead of it. It deliberately does NOT rate limit: a per-IP bucket behind Zeabur's proxy bounds an IP header this repo cannot measure, and the token makes the anonymous case moot. It also says nothing about whether the deterministic path stays open — that is every other case in the suite, all of which run with no token configured and stay green, which is the evidence that extraction is untouched.
